question: The displacement of a moving particle is $s(t)=t^3-9t^2+24t$ metres.(a) Calculate its velocity and acceleration at $t=2$ seconds.(b) Describe the state of motion of the particle at that instant.
explanation: Velocity from displacement$$v(t)=\frac{ds}{dt}=3t^2-18t+24$$At $t=2$,$$v(2)=3(2)^2-18(2)+24=12-36+24=0$$Acceleration from velocity$$a(t)=\frac{dv}{dt}=6t-18$$At $t=2$,$$a(2)=6(2)-18=-6\text{ m/s}^2$$Interpretation of velocitySince $v(2)=0$, the particle is momentarily at rest at $t=2$ seconds.Interpretation of accelerationThe negative acceleration indicates that the velocity is decreasing at this instant.Final resultThe velocity is $0$ m/s and the acceleration is $-6$ m/s$^2$.

options.A:
(a) $v=0$ m/s, $a=6$ m/s$^2$
(b) Momentarily at rest with positive acceleration
options.B:
(a) $v=-6$ m/s, $a=0$ m/s$^2$
(b) Moving in the negative direction
options.C:
(a) $v=6$ m/s, $a=-6$ m/s$^2$
(b) Moving in the positive direction
options.D:
(a) $v=0$ m/s, $a=-6$ m/s$^2$
(b) Momentarily at rest with negative acceleration
